use: Advisory triage data for model or human security review of a diff (EP-17). It orders, filters and words a review report. It is never a waiver: no entry clears a gate finding, changes a gate verdict, or keeps a path out of a gate. A finding a gate raised is cleared only by a person's committed waiver. Wording changes are caught by review, not by the loader.

path_exclusions.text: Test code does not ship to production. CI-facing test and build config (conftest.py, pytest.ini, tox.ini, setup.py, package.json, and the like) stays in scope, and a real secret in a test file is still a finding (scan-secrets judges every path).
Human documentation under docs/ is not shipped code. Agent instruction files and a docs build config (conf.py) are never excluded, wherever they sit.
Generated output is reviewed at its generator; report the generator input instead.
Vendored code is reviewed upstream; a pinned version known to be compromised is still a finding.

finding_exclusions.text: Denial of service, rate limiting, and memory or CPU exhaustion.
finding_exclusions.unless: the exhaustion is unbounded agent or model spend

finding_exclusions.text: Input validation that is missing but has no proven security impact.
Workflow inputs a person supplies when starting a CI run.
finding_exclusions.unless: the workflow can be started by an untrusted actor (a fork pull request, an issue or comment event, or a run chained from one)

finding_exclusions.text: Races and timing issues with no concrete path to a security effect.
finding_exclusions.unless: a secret, token or signature is compared in non-constant time

finding_exclusions.text: A dependency that is merely behind its latest release.
finding_exclusions.unless: the version is on a known-compromised list, or a security bump updated one manifest and left another on the old version
the code is inside an unsafe block or reinterprets raw memory

finding_exclusions.text: Server-side request forgery where the attacker controls only the path, not the host or scheme.
Regex injection. Catastrophic backtracking is denial of service and falls under that exclusion.

precedents.text: Environment variables and command-line flags are trusted input.
precedents.unless: a model, a tool result or a CI event payload fills them

precedents.text: Random (version 4) UUIDs can be assumed unguessable.
precedents.unless: the id is time-based, sequential or derived from user data

precedents.text: A missing permission check in client-side code is not a finding; the server must enforce it.
Templates and UI frameworks that escape output by default are XSS only where code uses the framework's explicit raw-HTML bypass.
Logging URLs is safe; logging a high-value secret in plaintext is a finding.
Report a MEDIUM finding only when it is obvious and concrete.
Command injection in notebooks and local shell scripts is rarely exploitable.
precedents.unless: the script runs in CI on event data, or as a package install or lifecycle hook

not_adopted.upstream: secrets or sensitive data stored on disk
not_adopted.why: A secret in a tracked file is a finding here: scan-secrets refuses it at commit.
Untrusted content reaching a model or a tool sink is in scope (injection-defense; record 12 section 8).
A removed or missing hard mitigation is a finding (record 12 sections 5 and 7).
Agent instruction and skill files are executable for an agent; only docs/ is excluded, and never_excluded wins.
An open redirect on an auth or OAuth flow leaks tokens; Claude Security lists it as a finding type.
